studies.label: Study 2 (AI dependence manipulation, AUT with ChatGPT)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2, Participants; actual sample reiterated in Sample size justification
counts_source.quote: A total of 132 university students (including graduate students; 51 males, 81 females) were recruited and randomly assigned to either the high-dependence group (n = 66) or the low-dependence group (n = 66).

arms.name: High AI dependence
arms.description: Priming tasks required ChatGPT-generated answers, with an instruction that AI answers were optimal. During the scored AUT, participants used ChatGPT and were instructed to directly adopt its creative solutions (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2).

arms.name: Low AI dependence
arms.description: Priming tasks were completed independently without external tools. During the scored AUT, participants used ChatGPT only as a supplementary reference and were instructed to independently complete their final solutions (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2).

studies.country: China; Qufu Normal University, Shandong (institution named in PDF p. 3; PDF p. 12 states that all participants came from a single institution).
studies.task: Generate as many innovative uses as possible for a tennis racket and a water pipe in an Alternative Uses Task framed as a creative competition.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (model/version not stated)

estimates.outcome: AUT creativity index (Consensual Assessment Technique, mean of raters)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Three trained psychology graduate students, blind to condition, independently scored novelty, appropriateness, and fluency on seven-point Likert scales. The mean of the raters’ scores was the creativity index. The report describes calibration of the raters but does not spell out aggregation across individual ideas, dimensions, and the two AUT objects (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2, Measures).

stats.difference_is: Printed total effect c of high versus low AI dependence (treatment minus control), from the mediation paragraph; not computed from the means.

estimates.notes: The arm names and direction follow the reconciled form: high dependence is treatment. The printed positive t and Cohen’s d describe low minus high dependence, the reverse of treatment minus control; their signs are preserved exactly. The negative total effect c is printed separately and is retained as the overall contrast, not the direct effect adjusted for critical thinking. The bootstrap interval in that paragraph is for the indirect effect and is not an interval for this contrast. Counts use the paper’s stated actual sample; no exclusions or separate post-exclusion counts are reported, and no counts were reconstructed from degrees of freedom. The analysis uses the averaged-rater creativity index and an independent-samples comparison of people, so unit, SD level, and uncertainty basis are coded participant. Both arms use ChatGPT on the AUT; the contrast also bundles different earlier priming experiences. Expert-rater coding follows the trained psychology graduate raters and the paper’s later description of the same measure as expert-rated creativity. Figure 3 contains raster-only mediation-path labels that differ from the prose; those labels were inspected but were not transcribed as statistics.

not_extracted.what: Study 1 (cross-sectional survey), including self-reported creativity, AI dependence, critical thinking, correlations, and mediation analyses
not_extracted.reason: No random assignment and no creativity scored on produced output. The creativity questionnaire measures self-perceived creative capacity (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 2.1-2.3, Table 1 and Figure 2).
Self-report manipulation check, not an outcome scored on creative output (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2-3.3 and Table 2).
Chinese Critical Thinking Structure Scale questionnaire, measured as in Study 1; not a scored-output creativity or convergent-test outcome (PDF p. 3, Measures; PDF p. 6, Measures and Table 2).
Self-report alternative mediator rather than a score on participants’ creative output (PDF p. 6, Measures and Table 2).

not_extracted.what: Study 2 critical-thinking and self-efficacy mediation paths, direct effects adjusted for the mediator, and indirect effects
not_extracted.reason: Mediation analyses and effects conditioned on post-treatment mediator measures are excluded. Only the printed overall total effect is retained with the eligible unadjusted creativity contrast (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 3.3 and Figure 3).

not_extracted.what: Study 3, including AUT creativity (S3-O1), manipulation checks, critical thinking, orientation-specific simple effects, and moderated mediation
not_extracted.reason: Random assignment is stated, but the creative-task AI intervention is unconfirmed. The methods name AI investment advice in a preliminary trust game and then say only that the AUT was identical to Study 2; they do not specify a generative model, AI availability during the AUT, or condition-specific AI-use instructions. Accordingly, the reconciled form leaves question, AI availability, and comparison type unresolved, and the study cannot yet be included as a randomized generative-AI assistance contrast. The full-sample creativity terms are in Table 4, Model 2; Model 3 and the orientation-specific comparisons are moderation analyses, and Table 5 is moderated mediation. Questionnaire outcomes also fail the output-scoring criterion. See PDF pp. 7-10, Sections 4.2-4.3 and Tables 3-5. The necessary supplementary task instructions were not available on file and could not be retrieved.

open_items: Study 3 requires the supplementary task instructions to establish whether participants used generative AI during the AUT and whether that use differed by randomized arm. The main text alone does not settle eligibility, question, or comparison type (PDF pp. 7-8; supplementary-materials listing on PDF p. 13).

No supplement is saved in the local supplement manifest. In this job, Python urllib requests to the named MDPI supplement URL and Europe PMC fullTextXML API both failed with WinError 10013 (network socket access forbidden); no supplement contents were verified.
The ChatGPT model/version and its release year are not specified; ai_tool.year is null.

Study 2 does not state the standardizer used for the printed Cohen’s d. Participant-level arm SDs are available, but the detailed aggregation of ratings across AUT ideas, objects, and dimensions is not described.

No separate results are printed for AUT novelty, appropriateness, or fluency; only the combined creativity index is available. No SE or confidence interval is printed for the eligible overall creativity contrast.
The raster mediation diagram in Figure 3 does not agree with the numerical paths in Section 3.3. The extraction uses the text and Table 2 without correcting either source.
notes: Extracted by B on 2026-10-10. Study identifiers preserve the paper and screening form: only S2 currently meets the extraction criteria; S1 and unresolved S3 are documented in not_extracted. The full markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks, including references and end matter, and all PDF pages were read with pymupdf. Tables 1-5 and Figures 1-3 were reviewed before final coding; the PDF has no appendix or embedded supplement. Inventory of eligible creativity statistics: both arm means and SDs, independent-samples t and degrees of freedom, bounded p-value, Cohen’s d, and the printed overall total effect c, all retained in one contrast. No values were estimated from figures or computed. The original printed precision is preserved in the source quotes. No diversity or delayed unassisted creative-output outcome is reported. The randomization and actual-sample statements support the recorded people counts; the form reports no shared participant sample with another paper.
